title: SQL Fundamentals for Data Analysts: UI Foundations
description: A short, beginner-focused course that introduces data analysts to browsing, sorting, and filtering e-commerce data in a database browser before any SQL is written.
target_audience: Beginner data analysts with no SQL experience

videos.title: Browse the Customers Table
videos.learning_objective: The learner navigates a database browser interface and recognizes how a table organizes records into rows and columns.
videos.discovery_objective: Open the Customers table in the Browse Data tab, identify the 4 columns by name, scroll through the first page of rows, and explain what each column represents.

exercise_artifact.description: A small e-commerce dataset with a Customers table and an Orders table linked by customer_id, spanning multiple countries and 12+ months of order history.

videos.new_capability: Open the Customers table in the Browse Data tab
videos.key_concept: A database table is like a filing cabinet drawer: every folder (row) has the same labeled tabs (columns), here holding one customer per folder.
videos.prerequisite_knowledge: None - this is the first video in the course.
videos.running_example_usage: Introduces the Customers table, which will be joined to Orders later in the course.
videos.proof_numbers: The Customers table contains 50 rows and 4 columns: customer_id, customer_name, country, and signup_date.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll sort the Orders table by order_amount in ascending order using the column header in the Browse Data tab.

videos.title: Sort the Orders Table by Amount in Ascending Order
videos.learning_objective: The learner uses column-header sorting to answer a real question about which order was smallest, without altering the underlying data.
videos.discovery_objective: Sort the Orders table by order_amount in ascending order using the column header in the Browse Data tab.

exercise_artifact.description: A small e-commerce dataset with a Customers table and an Orders table linked by customer_id, spanning multiple countries and 12+ months of order history.

videos.new_capability: Sort the Orders table by order_amount in ascending order
videos.key_concept: Sorting reorders rows for viewing purposes, like reshuffling a stack of receipts by price without changing any receipt's contents.
videos.prerequisite_knowledge: The learner knows how to open a table in the Browse Data tab from the previous video.
videos.running_example_usage: Uses the Orders table's order_amount column to surface the lowest-value order among 500 rows.
videos.proof_numbers: After sorting ascending, the lowest order_amount is $8.50, now at the top of 500 rows.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we opened the Customers table and saw 50 rows across 4 columns: customer_id, customer_name, country, and signup_date.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll filter the Orders table by status equal to Shipped using the filter box in the Browse Data tab.

videos.title: Filter the Orders Table by Status
videos.learning_objective: The learner filters rows by an exact text match to isolate a meaningful subset of orders for analysis.
videos.discovery_objective: Filter the Orders table so only rows with status equal to Shipped appear, using the filter box in the Browse Data tab.

exercise_artifact.description: A small e-commerce dataset with a Customers table and an Orders table linked by customer_id, spanning multiple countries and 12+ months of order history.

videos.new_capability: Filter the Orders table by exact text match on status
videos.key_concept: Filtering hides non-matching rows temporarily, like a sieve that only lets through grains of a certain size while the rest stays behind.
videos.prerequisite_knowledge: The learner knows how to sort a column in the Browse Data tab from the previous video.
videos.running_example_usage: Uses the Orders table's status column, which includes some NULL values for orders that were never marked with a status.
videos.proof_numbers: Filtering to status = 'Shipped' returns 210 of the 500 orders.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we sorted 500 orders by order_amount ascending and found the smallest order at $8.50.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll filter the Orders table by order_amount greater than 100 using the filter box in the Browse Data tab.

videos.title: Filter the Orders Table by Amount
videos.learning_objective: The learner filters rows by a numeric comparison to isolate higher-value orders for analysis.
videos.discovery_objective: Filter the Orders table so only rows with order_amount greater than 100 appear, using the filter box in the Browse Data tab.

exercise_artifact.description: A small e-commerce dataset with a Customers table and an Orders table linked by customer_id, spanning multiple countries and 12+ months of order history.

videos.new_capability: Filter the Orders table by numeric comparison on order_amount
videos.key_concept: Numeric filters use comparison operators to draw a line at a threshold, like setting a minimum price cutoff when shopping online.
videos.prerequisite_knowledge: The learner knows how to filter by exact text match from the previous video.
videos.running_example_usage: Uses the Orders table's order_amount column to isolate higher-value orders out of the full 500-row set.
videos.proof_numbers: Filtering to order_amount > 100 returns 187 of the 500 orders.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we filtered the Orders table to status = 'Shipped' and saw 210 of the 500 orders match.

running_example.name: E-Commerce Orders and Customers
running_example.description: A small e-commerce dataset with a Customers table and an Orders table linked by customer_id, spanning multiple countries and 12+ months of order history.
